findings.claim: No document states what the player is trying to achieve in Epoch 1, how they know they are winning, or what failure is; the only success-shaped object is a mechanism list, and the only loss-shaped events (trial, extraction) are hazards with no campaign-level fail state.

evidence.quote: Prevents optimizing a single score.

findings.bites_when: 05e/06 land and the player can walk and talk but nothing tells them which of 4 threads, 4 offices, 3 stocks matters or when an Epoch ends.
findings.disconfirm: Grepped DESIGN_NOTES.md and config.yaml for victory, win, game over, objective, goal, score: only anti-objective statements and the Epoch 1 'climax' mention. Epoch end condition is never defined (what ends Epoch 1: watch budget, thread resolution, player choice?).
findings.recommendation: Write a one-page Epoch 1 player contract: a stated mission in-fiction (e.g. 'Sorrel is not burned and the Gorge is not owned by one faction by watch N'), 3-4 visible measures, an end trigger, and two fail/partial outcomes that still carry forward as scars. Do this before 06.
findings.ignore_cost: The campaign is a toolbox of systems with no aim; every later tuning argument (pacing envelopes, storyteller) has no target to tune against.

findings.claim: The design has no player-facing feedback loop for covert action results: discovery layers, pressure stocks, and persecution risk are simulation state, and the notes specify no surface that tells the player an action worked, was noticed, or backfired, while explicitly banning HUD-style readouts.

evidence.quote: Triggered when `discoveryLayer >= 'attributed'`

findings.bites_when: first time an illicit instrument or letter is dispatched: consequences arrive hours later via Knock/Silent Wrong Action with no causal trail the player can read.
findings.disconfirm: Looked for a journal, dossier, after-action, consequence report, advisor debrief. The Ending/Lamp are described as characters who argue and sulk, and the Wider World Overview as a rumor/spoof board; none is assigned the job of 'telling you what your last move did'. Silent Wrong Action is literally a designed non-feedback mode.
findings.recommendation: Assign explicit feedback duties: The Ending delivers a per-watch statistical debrief (which fits its persona), The Lamp reports the bodily/room reading, and every WorldEffect carries a player-readable 'cause' string surfaced after the delay. Design a 'what happened because of me' ledger on the writing desk. Prototype it on the 2-room slice with 1 fake delayed effect.
findings.ignore_cost: Cultist Simulator / CK3 failure mode: player cannot attribute outcomes, concludes the game is random, disengages.

findings.claim: The minute-to-minute loop of Epoch 1 cannot be reconstructed from the docs: embodied walking and talking costs zero campaign time and the actions that do advance campaign time are a list of nouns with no verbs-and-decisions description.

evidence.quote: Reading costs no watch.
resting/studying in Chambers, waiting on or expediting correspondence
This loop does not advance `elapsedWatches` or inject storylets.

findings.bites_when: 05b ships the clocks: the player must choose between walking to talk to NPCs (free, no macro effect) and spending watches; nothing says why one beats the other.
findings.disconfirm: Best reconstruction: every 30-120 s walk to an NPC, Space, read chunks, pick a response row; every few minutes return to Chambers to write a letter or hold court, which spends watches; the Storyteller releases threads. Hunted for any sentence connecting these into a decision cycle; none. Lines 72 (requiresExternalTrigger) hint NPCs wait on the player, which is the closest link.
findings.recommendation: Write the loop as three stated cycles: minute (approach, read, choose, observe a reaction), session (one thread beat from omen to a visible consequence in about 45 min), epoch (acts I-III). Make talking cost an attention budget (limited NPC access per watch) so it competes with time-spend.
findings.ignore_cost: 05d-07 get built as isolated mechanics and the loop emerges by accident or not at all.

findings.claim: Agency is split into two halves with only a weak, undeclared coupling: Clock 1 (walk, talk, eavesdrop) is specified in great control detail, Clock 2 macro levers (offices, funds, letters, orbital) are specified as schemas, and the notes never say that a conversation outcome should change a macro lever or vice versa beyond generic WorldEffects.

evidence.quote: would burn out in 15 minutes
An ambient line does not spend a watch.

findings.bites_when: 07b/07c: pretext and fund rows appear in conversations; if they are the only bridge the economy is a menu item in dialogue, and Writing Desk/orbital play is a separate game.
findings.disconfirm: Section 7c and 7b do put pretext and fund spending on conversation rows, and regard gates Desk enclosures (line 118), so there are bridges. But the bridges are stated as data hooks, not as an intended experience.
findings.recommendation: Declare one rule: every macro lever is exercised through a person you physically find (letters are handed to a courier you walk to; funds spent in a conversation; orbital drop needs a place you stand). Fewer abstract menus.
findings.ignore_cost: Two games in one window: a walking sim plus a spreadsheet, with the second dominating.

findings.claim: There is no first-10-minutes or onboarding design: nothing says what the player sees, is told, or does on first opening Epoch 1, nor how the lace/advisors teach the systems.

findings.disconfirm: grep tutorial/onboard/first-time/opening: no hits in DESIGN_NOTES.md or config.yaml.
findings.recommendation: Script the opening 10 minutes as content: arrival cutscene still, the Lamp's first line, one thread omen in the yard, one person to talk to, one irreversible small choice with a visible consequence within 10 minutes (Disco Elysium / Pentiment prologues).
findings.ignore_cost: Friends bounce at minute 3; owner has no sense of which systems the player even perceives.

findings.claim: Design notes give far more attention to mechanism than experience: the Epoch 1 slice names 4 threads, 5+ rival tells, 6 romance discovery channels, 4 assassination vectors, 5 contingencies, but never says what moment-to-moment feeling or what memorable scene each should create.

findings.bites_when: content authoring starts for Sorrel/Pell/Vane: systems exist but no statement of the target emotion, so authoring is directed by schema coverage.
findings.disconfirm: Tone benchmarks (lines 36-48) and character exemplars show real experiential writing (Mara's one bad nail per keg is the standard). The gap is at the system and loop level, not the character level.
findings.recommendation: For each of Threads A-D write a 5-line 'best-case play story' (what the player does, sees, regrets). Use these as acceptance scenarios for 06 instead of tests of mechanism coverage.
findings.ignore_cost: Systems exist and cannot be judged fun or not; scope pressure then removes the wrong ones.

unconsidered_routes.title: Make the advisors the feedback channel
unconsidered_routes.proposal: The Ending produces a delayed 'integral' debrief after each watch (expected lives, with its odd probabilities), and The Lamp reports the physical truth of the room. Their disagreement is the player's readout of whether an action worked, was noticed, or backfired. Sulk and omission then become information-quality knobs, not only flavor.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Hades/Disco Elysium skill voices; Pentiment's after-the-fact reporting; Frostpunk's law/report ledger
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Replaces the unassigned 'how does the player learn' with the existing AdvisoryDuel; makes 07d consequential.

unconsidered_routes.title: One thread, one vertical slice, one full epoch-shaped loop first
unconsidered_routes.proposal: Before building offices/funds/rivals, hand-author Thread B (Sorrel/Pell) end-to-end with 6-8 people, 3 rooms and a visible consequence at the end, with an extraction-style end card. Judge fun with friends, then generalize.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Pentiment's single-case structure; Hitman level as a sandbox with a clear target
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Changes sequencing: 05b-06c are justified by a played thread rather than a schema list.

unconsidered_routes.title: Case-file / evidence-board layer for watching consequences
unconsidered_routes.proposal: A diegetic wax-and-string board on the Chambers wall, auto-populated by player actions and their discovered effects, showing which of your acts have been noticed and by whom.
unconsidered_routes.reference: Shadows of Doubt case board; Hitman's mission feedback; Cultist Simulator's slow verbs
unconsidered_routes.replaces_or_changes: Gives the discovery layers a player-facing form without a HUD.
